entries.name: Superpowers
entries.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
entries.covers: Methodology pack: brainstorm -> plan -> execute with subagents, TDD, debugging, verification, code review, worktrees, skill writing.
entries.compat: Claude Code plugin (official marketplace), Cursor plugin (/add-plugin superpowers), generic SKILL.md
entries.install: Claude Code: /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official ; individual: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git and copy skills/<slug> into /home/box/shared-skills/<slug>
entries.fit_reason: writing-plans/executing-plans are the mr Opus-plans/cheap-implements split; verification stops cheap models overclaiming.
entries.overlap: Already available to Grok Bot as skills; not in /home/box/shared-skills, so Claude Code/cursor-agent may lack them. Skip using-superpowers (asserts precedence).

skipped_on_install.reason: Requires a git worktree for every plan (conflicts with house rule: worktree only when parallel/large/risky) and hard-depends on scripts in subagent-driven-development plus finishing-a-development-branch, which are not installed.

entries.name: Matt Pocock's skills
entries.author: Matt Pocock (mattpocock)
entries.covers: Small, user-invoked engineering skills: grill a plan, turn a chat into a spec/tickets, implement a spec, TDD, bug diagnosis, handoff.
entries.compat: Claude Code plugin, generic SKILL.md (npx skills -a cursor)
entries.install: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a cursor  (choose picks + setup-matt-pocock-skills); Claude Code: claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official
entries.fit_reason: Spec-first loop (grill -> to-spec -> implement-spec) with near-zero context cost: skills are disable-model-invocation (slash-only).
entries.overlap: to-spec/implement-spec overlap superpowers writing-plans/executing-plans; to-spec publishes to the issue tracker (external side effect), so confirm before use.

skipped_on_install.reason: Mandates a worktree + branch per ticket with merger subagents, may open a draft PR, and depends on tdd, code-review, to-tickets and setup-matt-pocock-skills (not installed).

entries.name: pstack (Poteto's stack)
entries.author: Lauren Tan (poteto); standalone mirror backnotprop/pstack; Claude port michael-denyer/pstack-claude
entries.covers: Router skill /poteto-mode picks one of 23 playbooks (bug fix, feature, perf, multi-phase plan, babysit, shipping, autopilot) and pulls in ~60 workflow and principle skills; model roles set by /setup-pstack.
entries.compat: Cursor plugin (canonical); Claude Code/Codex via mirrors (npx skills add backnotprop/pstack; /plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins)
entries.install: Cursor: /add-plugin pstack then /setup-pstack ; Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins then /plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins
entries.fit_reason: Rigorous and model-role-aware like mr, but heavy (61 skills), defaults judgment to Opus, and has autonomous ship/autopilot playbooks. Pack score unchanged; its formal-verification skills (/statechart, /create-formal-verification-skill) are scored separately as pstack-statechart (29).
entries.overlap: tdd, reflect, planning, verification overlap superpowers; references cursor-team-kit.

entries.name: pstack /statechart + /create-formal-verification-skill
entries.author: Lauren Tan (poteto)
entries.covers: Model-check a small TLA+ model of a state machine or protocol with the real TLC checker (tla2tools 1.7.4), then compile TLC's state-graph dump into a small IR and emit a Mermaid stateDiagram (chart.mmd) plus a plain-English report of the shortest path to each broken rule. create-formal-verification-skill picks a high-risk target in a repo, verifies one property, and writes a project-local verify skill; maintain-formal-verification-skill keeps it in sync.
entries.compat: Generic SKILL.md folders (slash-only). Needs Node >=22.18 (or Bun/Deno) and Java 11+ with tla2tools.jar (auto-installed by mise on first run, or set TLA2TOOLS and JAVA). Rendering to SVG uses npm pele@1.9.0.
entries.install: Copy cursor/plugins/pstack/skills/statechart and .../create-formal-verification-skill into /home/box/shared-skills/<slug>. On this box run with TLA2TOOLS=/workspace/tools/tla/tla2tools.jar JAVA=/workspace/tools/tla/jdk-21.0.13+9-jre/bin/java (box-local, set up 2026-10-30).
entries.fit_reason: Finds ordering bugs (races, lost messages, stuck states) that tests miss in designs like stop-chat, ChatDO run leasing and the buying task FSM. Trial on the stop-chat spec (2026-10-30) found both seeded bugs in ~3 s and passed the fixed design. Slash-only, so zero always-on context. create-formal-verification-skill alone scores 26 (R=2: it writes a project-local skill into the repo).
entries.overlap: None installed. Adjacent: superpowers systematic-debugging, Trail of Bits property-based-testing.
entries.gate_note: Soft gate: needs Java + TLC (a runtime not on the box by default). Already satisfied on this box without root (JRE + checksum-verified jar in /workspace/tools/tla). No API key, no git writes, no Opus.
entries.status: qualifies (>=18, no hard gate); awaiting Rohan's go-ahead before install

installed_notes: grilling installed as a required dependency of grill-me (grill-me only calls the grilling skill).

to-spec is slash-only; it publishes the spec to the repo's issue tracker (gh issue create or local .scratch markdown) as configured by setup-matt-pocock-skills (not installed). Without that config it asks the user. Confirm before publishing.

writing-plans, verification-before-completion, systematic-debugging are linked into ~/.claude/skills only: cursor-agent already loads the same names from the cached superpowers 6.1.1 Cursor plugin, so a second copy would duplicate them. Shared copies are upstream v7.0.1 (newer).
writing-plans' handoff offers subagent-driven-development or executing-plans; on Claude Code neither is installed from shared-skills, so execute the plan inline.
